key_insight: Laser oscillation trajectories shape molten-pool heat distribution and flow, with well-designed paths improving droplet-transfer and weld-formation stability in aluminum double-wire welding.
engineering_relevance: Coordinating laser power, oscillation settings, and wire feed offers a route to more stable, high-quality aluminum welds.
method: Investigate coupled effects of laser power, oscillation frequency, amplitude, trajectory, and wire-feed speed.
Use high-speed imaging to observe molten-pool surface flow, droplet transfer, and metal filling.
Compare oscillation paths and seek links between energy input, pool behavior, and forming quality.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports real-time high-speed observations and qualitative trajectory-dependent changes in pool behavior, but provides no numerical performance metrics.
watch_item: The coupled model remains a stated research aim, and the abstract does not demonstrate AI-based optimization or validated process-control performance.
paper_title: Study on the transition behavior and forming process of oscillating laser double-wire welding of aluminum alloy
